# Temple Scroll Column 30 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 30 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**30:1** You shall construct an outer court. On the south side, the outer court shall extend one thousand six hundred cubits in length, from corner to corner.

**30:2** It shall run from the southeastern corner westward along the south side to the southwestern corner.

**30:3** You shall make three gates on the south side, spaced at equal intervals from one another and from the corners.

**30:4** The gates shall be forty-two cubits wide and twenty-eight cubits high to the lintel.

**30:5** Each gate shall have a portico forty-two cubits wide and twenty-eight cubits deep, with towers rising above the gates.

**30:6** On the east side, the outer court shall extend one thousand six hundred cubits in length, from corner to corner.

**30:7** It shall run from the southeastern corner northward along the east side to the northeastern corner.

**30:8** You shall make three gates on the east side, spaced at equal intervals from one another and from the corners.

**30:9** The gates shall conform to the same dimensions: forty-two cubits wide and twenty-eight cubits high.

**30:10** Each gate shall have a portico of identical dimensions, with towers rising above.

**30:11** On the north side, the outer court shall extend one thousand six hundred cubits, from the northeastern corner westward to the northwestern corner.

**30:12** You shall make three gates on the north side, at equal intervals from one another and from the corners, conforming to the same dimensions.

**30:13** On the west side, the outer court shall extend one thousand six hundred cubits, from the northwestern corner southward to the southwestern corner.

**30:14** You shall make three gates on the west side, at equal intervals from one another and from the corners, conforming to the same dimensions.

**30:15** The total perimeter of the outer court shall measure six thousand four hundred cubits, forming a square from corner to corner.

**30:16** The wall of the outer court shall be seven cubits thick and forty-nine cubits high, constructed upon a foundation of dressed stone sunk three cubits into the ground.

---

*LOGOS notes: Column 30 well preserved. The outer court introduces the third and largest concentric ring of the temple complex. At 1,600 cubits per side (approximately 730 meters), this court far exceeds the dimensions of any historical temple compound. The twelve gates (three per side) correspond to the twelve tribes of Israel, as confirmed in later columns. Gate proportions: 42 cubits wide by 28 high (ratio 3:2). Wall height of 49 cubits (7 squared) reflects the Temple Scroll's pervasive heptadic symbolism.*
